answer: Let bonded collateral B per vertex identity be slashed quadratically, so k Sybil identities require super-linear capital C(k)=alpha sum i^2 plus zero-knowledge verifiable delay fees. A Sybil jetty expands only when marginal extraction dV/dk=beta/(2sqrt(k)) exceeds marginal cost dC/dk=2alpha k; at the capital summit this inequality reverses, making expected attack utility negative. Thus no cluster can cross the consensus threshold at positive net payoff, yielding a robust Nash equilibrium.
